jess-support: Heads-up — ACME reported a production failure when using structured output (json mode) with streaming enabled. Their client gets a JSON parse error from our response body.

alex-support: Can you paste the original response snippet + request_id?

jess-support: Request ID: req_0a7c3b. Here's the raw chunks we captured from the server (we only sanitized tokens):
```
chunk 1: {"choices":[{"message":{"content":{"type":"structured","value":"{\"title\":\"Summary\",\"body\":\"Line1\
""}}}]}
chunk 2: {\"text\":\"Line2\"}\"}}]}
```
Notice chunk 1 ends with a backslash-newline escape sequence boundary. When the client concatenates chunks naive the escape becomes a literal newline in the JSON string and the downstream parser throws `Unexpected token` at the start of the newline.

acme-cust: Repro steps (simplified): curl our /v1/responses stream -> read chunks and join -> JSON.parse(body) -> fails on our end consistently for long outputs with embedded newlines. We can share a minimal reproducer if helpful.

alex-support: Thanks. @mike-runtime any idea how streaming + structured serialization could produce an unescaped newline inside a JSON string?

mike-runtime: This is likely a chunk-boundary split of an escape sequence. We send the structured payload as a quoted JSON string (we escape newlines as `\n`). If the model / tokenizer emits a backslash and the next chunk starts with `n` or a CRLF, and our streaming serializer flushes between them, the concatenated bytes can end up as an actual newline instead of the two-character escape. The parser then sees an unescaped control char in a quoted string — invalid JSON.

sara-ml: Another vector: some models sometimes emit raw newlines inside string tokens (e.g., they produce a literal line break token instead of `\n`). If our serialization layer assumes all newline-like things are escaped, we break. We should check both the runtime chunk boundaries and the model token stream for literal newlines.

jess-support: Logged impact: multiple clients (2 major customers) hit this intermittently when responses are >2k chars and include multi-line fields (logs, stack traces). One customer uses a strict JSON parser and fails fast, causing retries and higher latency on their side.

mike-runtime: Immediate mitigation: set streaming to false for structured mode for affected customers (disable chunked SSE). That avoids splitting escape sequences. Also we can add a post-join sanitizer that scans for unescaped control characters in quoted values and re-escapes them — cheap quick fix.

leo-pm: Priority? ACME is on Dedicated and this blocks a live feature. Recommend: (1) quick mitigation (disable streaming per-customer), (2) hotfix in runtime to ensure we never emit a bare control char inside JSON strings when streaming, (3) broader test coverage.

alex-support: @acme-cust are you ok with us toggling streaming off for your workload temporarily?

acme-cust: Yes please, toggle it off. We can accept slightly higher latency over broken JSON. We also sent a small reproducible payload via support ticket 1369.

jess-support: Action items:
- alex-support: schedule toggle for ACME now (opt-out streaming for their API key)
- mike-runtime: patch runtime to detect trailing backslash at chunk end and avoid emitting it without the following char; add re-escape sanitizer on join (assign owner)
- sara-ml: check model emission for literal newline tokens on our model variants and list affected model versions
- leo-pm: prepare comms and risk assessment for disabling streaming as default fallback

mike-runtime: Quick repro we used locally:
```bash
# simulate chunk split of escape sequence
echo -n '{"value":"Line1\' > a.txt
# then simulate continuation chunk starting with n and more text
echo -n 'nLine2"}' >> a.txt
cat a.txt | python -c 'import sys,json;print(json.loads(sys.stdin.read()))'
# this throws a JSONDecodeError if the receiver doesn't treat \\n as two chars
```

sara-ml: Good tests. I'll run the model tokenizer across >1000 samples to see how often it emits literal newlines vs "\n" sequences.

deploy-bot: canary toggle created: canary/streaming-disabled/acme-cust -> rolled to 100% for customer key req_0a7c3b at 2025-11-02T14:30Z :white_check_mark:

alex-support: ACME confirms parser now succeeds after canary.

jess-support: Postmortem notes will include: root cause likely combination of streaming chunk boundary + model emission of backslash as last token, plus client-side naive join+parse. We need fixes at runtime + test harness + docs for clients about robust streaming parsing.

leo-pm: Assign owners and ETA: mike-runtime (hotfix in 48h), sara-ml (analysis in 72h), alex-support (customer comms done), jess-support (postmortem draft).

acme-cust: Thanks everyone — we'll monitor and report any regressions.

mike-runtime: I'll add a unit test that simulates escape split at every possible byte boundary and assert the joined output is always valid JSON for structured mode.

jess-support: Closing the escalation for now; re-open if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
